title: 7 Mathematics KCPE 2009
text:
THE KENYA NATIONAL EXAMINATION COUNCIL
 KCPE 2009
 654321
 MATHEMATICS
 READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS CAREFULLY Time : 2 hours
 1. You have been given this question booklet and a separate answer sheet. The question booklet
 contains 50 question.
 2. Do any necessary rough work in this booklet.
 3. When you have chosen your answer, mark it on the ANSWER SHEET, not in this question
 booklet.
 HOW TO USE THE ANSWER SHEET
 4. Use only an ordinary pencil.
 5. Mark sure that you have written on the answer sheet:
 YOUR INDEX NUMBER
 YOUR NAME
 NAME OF YOUR SCHOOL
 6. By drawing a dark line inside the correct numbered boxes mark your full Index Number ( i.e.
 School Code Number and the three figured Candidate’s Number) in the grid near the top of the
 answer sheet.
 7. Do not make any marks outside the boxes.
 8. Keep the sheet as clean as possible and do not fold it.
 9. For each of the question 1-50 four answer are given. Then answer are lettered A,B,C and D. In
 each case only ONE of the answers is correct. Choose the correct answer.
 10. On the answer sheet the correct answer is to be shown by drawing a dark line inside the box in
 which the letter have chosen is written.
 Example
 In the question booklet:
 11. What is the value of 6(24-18)+6x4?
 A. 30
 B. 25
 C. 10
 D. 28

 12. Your dark line MUST be within the box
 13. For each question ONLY ONE box is to be marked in each set of four boxes.
 The Kenyan Examination Council,2009.
 1. Which one of the following numbers is twenty six million, four hundred and thirty thousand,two
 hundred and nine in symbols?
 A. 26432009
 B. 2643209
 C. 26430309
 2. Which one of the following statement is correct?
 A. ¾ >0.75
 B. 1/9 <0.1
 C. 4/3 < 1.3
 D. 2/5 <0.5
 3. A storekeeper donated 5 tonnes of sugar to families in the vallage. Each family receive 2.5kg of
 sugar.
 How many families benefited?
 A. 20 000
 B. 2 000
 C. 200
 D. 20
 4. On the diagram below construct a perpendicular from R to cut PQ at S?
 A. 4.9cm

 6. Mwende had mangoes. She ate 5 and shared the remaining among her 6 friends. She however
 found that she needed 2 more mangoes. How many mangoes had she at the beginning?
 A. 22
 B. 27
 C. 29
 D. 31
 7. Maloba deposited Sh. 8000 in a financial institution that paid simple interest. At the end of 3
 years this money had amounted to Sh. 9200. At what rate per annum was the simple interest
 awarded?
 A. 5%
 B. 15%
 C. 38 ½ %
 D. 4 8/23%
 8. Adhiambo left home and cycled for 1 ½ hours at an Average speed of 8 km/h. She rested for 30
 minutes and continued with the journey for 2 hours at an average speed of 7 ½ km/h. What was
 the average speed for the whole journey.
 A. 27km/h
 B. 7 5/7 km/h
 C. 7 ¾ km/h
 D. 6 ¾ km/h
 9. The bar grap shows the number and the sizes of pairs of the shoes sold in one week.
 Which size of the shoe was brought most?
 A. 12
 B. 11
 C. 8
 D. 7

 A. 6
 B. 2100
 C. 3000
 D. 3900

 he work up?
 A. 6.15am
 B. 12.15am
 C. 12.15am
 D. 6.15pm

 15. If a shopkeeper sells a basin for sh. 72,he would make a loss of 10%. At what price must he sell
 the basin so that he makes a profit of 20%
 A. Sh. 96
 B. Sh. 86.40
 C. Sh. 80
 D. Sh. 79.20
 16. What is the value of 2w ( x -2 )2
 y+1 when
 x = 5, y = x + 3 and w = 2x + y?
 A. 12
 B. 24
 C. 36
 D. 144
 17. Below are two graphs. One graph shows the journey by a bus from Nairobi to Nakuru. The other
 shows the journey by a car from Nakuru to Nairobi.
 How far from Nakuru was the bus when the car reached Nairobi?
 A. 115km
 B. 90km
 C. 60km
 D. 35km
 18. In a meeting 3/5 of the attendants were women, ¼ of the remainder were men and the rest
 were children. There were 80 men in that meeting. How many children were there?
 A. 120
 B. 240
 C. 480
 D. 800
 19. What is the number 15.76 rounded off to the nearest tenth?
 A. 15.7
 B. 15.8
 C. 16
 D. 20
 20. What is the value of
 4/5 + 3/5 of ( 2/3 – 1/5) + ¾ × 2/5?
 A. 1 19/50
 B. 1 143/ 150
 C. 1 3/10
 D. 1 23/250
 21. A school contributed money for project as follows: Pupils in class 1 -4 contributed sh. 10 each,
 Pupils in class 5 -8 contributed sh. 20 each Teachers contributed sh. 200 each The head teacher
 contributed sh. 500. Each class in school was double streamed with 30 pupil per stream. The
 number of teachers included the head teacher was 26. How much money was contributed
 altogether?
 A. Sh. 12 700
 B. Sh. 15 100
 C. Sh. 19 900
 D. Sh. 20 100
 22. The table below shows the fare in shillings for a matatu travelling from Nairobi to Nakuru.
 Fourteen passengers boarded the matatu at Nairobi. Seven of the Passengers alighted at Gilgil
 while five others boarded at Gilgil for Nakuru. How much money altogether did the driver
 collect?
 A. Sh. 3650
 B. Sh. 3500
 C. Sh.3150
 D. Sh. 1900
 23. The table below shows the number of pupils who were in standards 1 to 4 in a certain school
 from 2001 to 2004
 Std 1 Std 2 Std 3 Std 4
 2001 79 73 59 55
 2002 83 77 71 57
 2003 86 80 74 68
 2004 89 83 77 71
 How many pupils of the class which was in Std 1 in 2001 had dropped out of the class by 2004?
 A. 24
 B. 16
 C. 10
 D. 6
 24. Matu paid sh. 7600 for a radio after getting a 5% discount on the marked price. How much
 would he have paid if he had been given a 15% discount?
 A. Sh. 8000
 B. Sh. 6800
 C. Sh. 6840
 D. Sh. 6460
 25. What is the value of s in the equation
 5/4 + 2( s + 5) =6?
 A. 2 10/11
 B. 1 1/11
 C. 10 2/11
 D. 2 4/9

 What is the mean number of pupil per class?
 A. 26
 B. 38
 C. 41
 D. 246
 27. What is the next number in the sequence
 6 , 13, 24, 37, ______?
 A. 58
 B. 56
 C. 54
 D. 52
 28. A rectangular container is 80cm long,50cm wide and 40 cm high. The container is filled with
 water to a level 30cm high. What is the volume of empty space in the container?
 A. 180 000cm3
 B. 160 000cm3
 C. 120 000cm3
 D. 40 000cm3
 29. A team of eleven players took lunch in a hotel, which offered food prices as shown in the table
 below.
 Ugali Rice Chips
 Beef Sh. 60 Sh. 65 Sh. 75
 Chicken Sh.70 Sh. 70 Sh. 100
 Fish Sh. 75 Sh. 80 Sh. 105
 5 players each took ugali with chicken
 3 players each took chips with fish
 The remaining players each took rice with beef Musa gave one thousand shilling note to pay for
 the lunch of all the players. What balance did he get?
 A. Sh. 55
 B. Sh. 115
 C. Sh. 310
 D. Sh. 885

 0.4

 32. Sera sells googs for a company. She is paid a salary of sh. 84 000 per month plus a commission
 of 20% for the sale of goods worth above sh. 10 000. In one month her total earing were sh. 150
 000. What was the value of the goods she sold?
 A. Sh. 760 000
 B. Sh. 340 000
 C. Sh. 330 000
 D. Sh. 244 000
 33. A father shared money among his three children Mulwa, Wangare and Achesa. Wangare
 received sh. 10 more than Achesa, While Mulwa got twice the amount of Wangare got. If Achesa
 received sh. X, which one of the following expression represents the total amount of the money
 given to the three children?
 A. 4x + 30
 B. 4x + 30
 C. 2x + 20
 D. 3x + 30
 34. In a class the ratio of the number of boys to girls is 2 : 3. What is the percentage of the number
 of boys in the class?
 A. 33 1/3 %
 B. 40%
 C. 60%
 D. 66 2/3%
 35. The diagram below is a net of asolid.
 If the net is folded, which one of the following diagrams represent the solid formed?
 36. The figure below represents a vegetable garden consisting of a square and four semicircles each
 of diameter 4.2m.
 What is the area of the garden in square metres? ( Take π = 22/7)
 A. 69.6
 B. 225
 C. 252.72
 D. 333.88
 37. What is the difference between the L.C.M. and the G.C.D. of the number 24, 32 and 40?
 A. 8
 B. 472
 C. 480
 D. 488
 38. A school offers only 4 games. Each pupil was asked to choose one favourite game out of the 4.
 0.4 of the pupils chose football
 0.2 of the pupil chose netball
 0.3 of the pupils chose basketball
 The rest, who were 112 pupils, chose hockey.
 What was the total number of the pupils who chose football and netball?
 A. 240
 B. 160
 C. 400
 D. 80
 39. A sales man had 2 240 litres of juice which she parcked in 500ml and 250ml packets. Three
 quarters of the juice was parked in 500ml packets and the restin 250ml packets.
 What was the total number of the packets used?
 A. 56
 B. 560
 C. 5600
 D. 56000
 40. A rectangular plot of the land has a perimeter of 35m. The longer side is 10m. A wall is to be
 constructed along one of the diagonals of the plot. What would be the length of the wall?
 A. 78 1/8m
 B. 171 ½ m
 C. 7 ½ m
 D. 12 ½ m
 41. Mary bought a T.V. a set on hire purchase terms. She paid a deposit of sh. 800 and 15 equal
 monthly instalments of sh. 700 each. The hire purchase price was 25% higher than the cash
 price. Amina bought the same T.V. set on cash. How much more than Amina did Mary pay for
 the T.V. set?
 A. Sh. 2 260
 B. Sh. 2 825
 C. Sh. 9 040
 D. Sh. 11 300
 42. In triangle PQR below, PQ =8cm,PM =MQ and PR =RQ =5cm.
 What is the area of the triangle PQR?
 5cm
 Q 5cm
 A. 7 ½ cm2
 B. 6cm2
 C. 12 ½ cm2
 D. 12cm2
 43. Eighteen people can take 72 days to complete the piece of work. If 2 of the people did not turn
 up for the work, how many more days would the remaining number of people, working at the
 same rate take to complete the work?
 A. 9
 B. 81
 C. 153
 D. 575
 44. Pupils in classes 5,6,7 and 8 to raise funds for a party. Class 7 raised sh. X while class 5 raised 1/3
 of what class 7 raised. Class 6 raised sh. 100 less than the total amount raised by both classes 5
 and 7. If the total amount was sh. 6 900, which one of the following equation can be used to find
 the amount raised by each class?
 A. X + 2/3x + 100 = 6900
 B. 3x + 2/3x + 300 = 6900
 C. 3x 2/3 x + 300 =6900
 D. 3x + 2/3x + 100 = 6900
